# Foundation Models (GeoFMs) {background-color="#2C5F77"}

## What & Why

- Pre-trained once with **self-supervision** on large, global EO archives
- Adapted to many tasks: **fine-tune** a head (or the whole model), or just use the **embeddings** as features
- Label-efficient: published benchmarks show useful results from small labelled sets, but how small depends on the task. Test on your own data before promising "100 labels"
- Global pre-training data includes Southeast Asia, but check how well your region and season are represented

---

## Traditional CNN vs Foundation Model

| | Train a CNN from scratch | Start from a GeoFM |
|---|---|---|
| Pre-training | none (or ImageNet) | self-supervised on global EO archives |
| Labels needed | many (thousands typical) | fewer: start small, measure, add more |
| Sensors | usually one, fixed bands | model-dependent: multi-sensor, any-band models exist |
| Compute to adapt | full training run | fine-tune a head / small model, or train a classifier on embeddings |
| Main risk | overfitting small data | domain shift (sensor, resolution, region) from the pre-training data |

---

## Why It Matters for the Philippines

- **Label scarcity:** few agencies hold large, consistent labelled datasets
- **Disaster tempo:** typhoon and flood products are needed within hours to days
- **Heterogeneous landscapes:** from Metro Manila to BARMM, plus persistent cloud cover (SAR-capable models help)
- **Budget efficiency:** one backbone (or one embedding dataset) reused for crops, mangroves and settlements

---

## Open GeoFMs You Can Use (Nov 2026) {.smaller}

| Model | Who / when | What it is | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Prithvi-EO-2.0** | IBM, NASA, Jülich SC · Dec 2024 | 300M / 600M ViT, masked autoencoder on **4.2M** global HLS time-series samples (30 m), temporal + location embeddings | [arXiv 2412.02732](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.02732), [IBM blog](https://research.ibm.com/blog/prithvi2-geospatial) |
| **Clay v1.5** | Clay · 2024 (trained Sep 2024) | MAE-based, any number of bands; trained on Sentinel-2, Landsat, Sentinel-1, NAIP, LINZ, MODIS; Apache-2.0 | [Clay v1.5 spec](https://clay-foundation.github.io/model/release-notes/specification.html) |
| **TerraMind 1.0** | IBM + ESA Φ-lab + Jülich SC · Apr 2025 | any-to-any **generative** multimodal model (S1, S2, DEM, land cover…), >9M samples; tiny/small edge versions Oct 2025 | [ESA](https://www.esa.int/Applications/Observing_the_Earth/ESA_and_IBM_collaborate_on_TerraMind), [Φ-lab](https://philab.esa.int/less-is-more-the-power-of-terramind-in-your-pocket-and-in-space/) |
| **Copernicus-FM** | TUM and partners · ICCV 2025 | extends DOFA to any Sentinel modality (S1, S2, S3, S5P); with Copernicus-Pretrain data and Copernicus-Bench | [GitHub](https://github.com/zhu-xlab/copernicus-fm) |
| **DOFA** | Xiong et al. · 2024 | "Dynamic One-For-All": wavelength-conditioned patch embedding, so one model serves optical, SAR, hyperspectral | [arXiv 2403.15356](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.15356) |
| **SatMAE** | Stanford · NeurIPS 2022 | early MAE for temporal + multispectral imagery (fMoW-Sentinel); a key ancestor of the models above | [project page](https://sustainlab-group.github.io/SatMAE/) |

Fine-tuning toolkit for Prithvi/TerraMind and many others: [TerraTorch](https://github.com/torchgeo/terratorch)

## The 2025–26 Shift: Embedding Datasets {.smaller}

Instead of running a model yourself, **download pre-computed embeddings** (one vector per 10 m pixel per year) and train a small classifier on them, like the Random Forest from Day 2.

| Dataset | Producer | Details | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Satellite Embedding V1** (AlphaEarth Foundations) | Google / Google DeepMind · Jul 2025 | 64-D, 10 m, annual, global land + coastal; in Earth Engine as `GOOGLE/SATELLITE_EMBEDDING/V1/ANNUAL` (bands `A00`–`A63`) | [EE catalog](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/GOOGLE_SATELLITE_EMBEDDING_V1_ANNUAL), [DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/blog/alphaearth-foundations-helps-map-our-planet-in-unprecedented-detail/), [paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22291) |
| **Tessera** | Univ. of Cambridge and partners · 2025 (CVPR 2026 paper) | Sentinel-1 + Sentinel-2, 10 m, annual embeddings 2017–2025, open, no registration | [ESA, Jun 2026](https://www.esa.int/Applications/Observing_the_Earth/Copernicus/Tessera_AI_model_offers_accessible_way_to_view_Earth) |
| **OlmoEarth v1.3** | Ai2 · Oct 2026 | S1 + S2 + Landsat year → 128-D vector per 10 m pixel (first 64 dims usable alone); global embeddings on Source Cooperative | [Ai2 blog](https://allenai.org/blog/olmoearth-v1-3) |

**Caveat:** embedding dimensions are not physically interpretable. Validate against local reference data before operational use.

---

## Embeddings in Practice (Earth Engine)

```python
import ee
ee.Initialize(project="your-cloud-project")   # EE now requires a Cloud project

aoi = ee.Geometry.Rectangle([124.36, 7.05, 125.63, 8.84])   # ~Bukidnon (bbox)
emb = (ee.ImageCollection("GOOGLE/SATELLITE_EMBEDDING/V1/ANNUAL")
         .filterDate("2024-01-01", "2025-01-01")
         .filterBounds(aoi)
         .mosaic())                                     # 64 bands: A00 … A63

training = emb.sampleRegions(collection=labelled_points,   # your field labels
                             properties=["class"], scale=10)
clf = ee.Classifier.smileRandomForest(100).train(training, "class", emb.bandNames())
landcover = emb.classify(clf).clip(aoi)
```

Same workflow as Day 2, but the 64 embedding bands replace the hand-made spectral features. Google's [tutorial series](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/tutorials/community/satellite-embedding-01-introduction) covers this in more detail.

---

## How a GeoFM Works

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["Large unlabelled EO archive"] --> B["Self-supervised pre-training<br/>(masking, contrastive, multimodal)"]
  B --> C["Foundation model"]
  C --> D["Fine-tune with a small labelled set"]
  C --> E["Or: export embeddings,<br/>train a light classifier"]
  D --> F["Task model: flood, crop, mangrove…"]
  E --> F
```

- Pre-train once (expensive, done by the model provider); adapt many times (cheap)

---

## Philippine Use Cases: Project Ideas {.smaller}

These are **illustrative project ideas** for discussion, not deployed systems. The numbers depend on your data.

- **Rapid flood mapping:** fine-tune Prithvi-EO-2.0 or TerraMind on Sentinel-1/-2 flood labels (start from public Sen1Floods11 checkpoints, add local Philippine events)
- **Crop and land-cover mapping:** Satellite Embedding / Tessera features + a few hundred DA/PSA field points → provincial crop map
- **Mangrove monitoring:** embeddings + DENR / NAMRIA reference plots, compared year to year for change
- **Drought (link to Session 2):** add embedding-derived land-cover masks to restrict NDVI forecasts to cropland

---

# On-board AI {background-color="#2C5F77"}

## AI in Orbit: Where We Are (Nov 2026) {.smaller}

- **Φsat-2 (ESA):** 6U CubeSat launched 16 Aug 2024 (Transporter-11); multispectral imager; entered operational phase in July 2025
  - On-board apps: cloud detection (discard cloudy scenes), image-to-street-map for disaster response, deep image compression, vessel detection, wildfire and marine-pollution monitoring
  - Source: [ESA EO Gateway, Jul 2025](https://earth.esa.int/eogateway/news/ai-enabled-satellite-enters-operational-phase)
- **GeoFMs in orbit:** a compressed Prithvi model ran flood and cloud detection on the Kanyini satellite and on Thales Alenia Space's IMAGIN-e payload on the ISS, the first GeoFM deployed in orbit ([NASA, May 2026](https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/ai-foundation-model-in-orbit/), [preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01181))
- **Edge-sized models:** tiny/small TerraMind and Prithvi variants for laptops, phones and satellites (Oct 2025, [IBM](https://research.ibm.com/blog/terramind-prithvi-tiny-small-models-geospatial))

**Why it matters:** less downlink and lower latency, which helps time-critical alerts (fires, floods, ships). Trade-off: smaller models, harder validation.

---

# Self-Supervised Learning {background-color="#2C5F77"}

## Why SSL for EO

- Only a tiny fraction of the satellite archive is labelled; SSL learns from the raw archive
- Cuts annotation cost and helps "cold-start" regions with few labels
- Produces representations reusable for segmentation, detection, forecasting, which is what makes GeoFMs possible

---

## Common SSL Strategies

- **Masked autoencoding:** hide most patches (often ~75%) and reconstruct them (SatMAE, Prithvi, Clay)
- **Contrastive learning:** pull together views of the same place/time, push apart others (SimCLR, MoCo); **self-distillation** variants need no negatives (BYOL, DINO)
- **Temporal pretext tasks:** order scenes, predict the next time step, detect anomalies
- **Cross-modal learning:** align or generate Sentinel-1 ↔ Sentinel-2 ↔ DEM (TerraMind, Copernicus-FM)

---

## Building an SSL Pipeline

1. Collect unlabelled Sentinel/Landsat imagery for your area of interest
2. Cloud/shadow filtering; tile into patches or time series
3. Choose a pretext objective (masked, contrastive, temporal)
4. Pre-train a backbone (ViT, CNN, LSTM) on GPUs
5. Fine-tune on mission-specific labels

**In practice:** before pre-training your own model, check whether an existing GeoFM or embedding dataset already covers your sensor and region.

---

# Explainable AI (XAI) {background-color="#2C5F77"}

## Why XAI

- Builds trust for operational agencies (DRRM, agriculture, enforcement)
- Reveals bias or drift (seasonal, regional, sensor)
- Supports governance and documentation requirements

---

## Techniques at a Glance

| Technique | Works With | Insight Provided |
|-----------|------------|------------------|
| **SHAP** | Tree models, tabular and deep models | Feature contribution per prediction |
| **LIME** | Any classifier/regressor | Local surrogate explaining one sample |
| **Grad-CAM** | CNN-based models | Heatmap of salient pixels/regions |
| **Integrated Gradients** | Differentiable models (incl. transformers, LSTMs) | Attribution along an input path |

Libraries: [SHAP](https://shap.readthedocs.io/en/latest/), [LIME](https://github.com/marcotcr/lime), [Captum](https://captum.ai/) (PyTorch)

---

## Applying XAI in EO

- **Flood mapping:** Grad-CAM over segmentation outputs to check the model looks at water, not shadows
- **Drought LSTM (Session 2):** Integrated Gradients to see which past months drive the forecast
- **Crop yield models:** SHAP to rank NDVI, rainfall, soil moisture drivers
- **Vessel alerts:** LIME on trajectory features to explain why a track was flagged
- Pair XAI outputs with review by local analysts (LGUs, NAMRIA, PAGASA)

---

## Philippine Integration Roadmap

1. **Assess:** audit data readiness, choose priority missions (floods, crops, mangroves)
2. **Adapt:** try embeddings first (cheapest); fine-tune a GeoFM if accuracy is not enough; label locally
3. **Deploy:** package as an API/dashboard; share models through national repositories such as DOST-ASTI's [DIMER](https://asti.dost.gov.ph/news-articles/dost-asti-dimer-platform-powers-real-world-ai-solutions/)
4. **Scale:** monitor drift with XAI, refresh labels, expand to new regions

---

## Key Takeaways

- **GeoFMs:** open models (Prithvi-EO-2.0, Clay, TerraMind, Copernicus-FM) cut the labels you need; how much depends on the task
- **Embeddings first:** Satellite Embedding, Tessera or OlmoEarth + a Random Forest is the cheapest way to start
- **On-board AI** is operational (Φsat-2) and GeoFMs have run in orbit: lower latency, harder validation
- **SSL** is what makes all of this possible; check existing models before pre-training your own
- **XAI** builds trust and catches models that look at the wrong thing; pair it with expert review

---

## Discussion & Q&A

- Where can GeoFMs or embeddings help your agency most?
- Data readiness and labelling strategies
- On-board vs ground processing: what latency do you actually need?
- Risks, governance, and explainability
